results.quote: Six stages in a chain: 1 at the source, 6 at the load.
absent (closest: "rounded down" and "Starting charge: 3, 6, 6, 2, 2, 1"; nothing says quantities are whole numbers that never go negative)
Ratings, stages 1 to 6: 10, 8, 12, 6, 9, 7.
Upper thresholds: 7, 6, 9, 5, 7, 5.
Lower thresholds: 3, 2, 4, 2, 3, 2.
Everything starts CLEAR; ground tally starts at zero. ... Starting charge: 3, 6, 6, 2, 2, 1.
Breaker setting: 38 total. ... ground tally starts at zero.
Every cycle runs five moves in order, each finished chain-wide before the next.
Charge in. Add the cycle's feed to each stage; ratings aren't enforced here.
Walk 1 to 6. A stage over rating dumps the excess into the next stage down and sits at exactly rating
Walking in order, 1's excess can tip 2 before you reach 2.
stage 6's excess goes to ground.
Read each stage now. CLEAR goes ASSERTED at or above its upper threshold
ASSERTED goes CLEAR at or below its lower.
In between it holds. Log every flip. (single read of each stage in one pass)
Take all six readings first, then move everything at once.
A CLEAR stage leaks a quarter, rounded down, to ground.
An ASSERTED stage sends half, rounded down, back through its return diode to the stage before; stage 1's goes to ground.
Ratings aren't checked here, so a stage can sit over until next cycle's shunts, or for good after cycle 5.
Sum the chain. Strictly over 38, every stage halves ... At 38 or under, nothing.
every stage halves, rounded down, the difference to ground; note the cycle.

the charge on stages 1 to 6, in order; the state of each stage ... every flip as (cycle, stage, state before, state after); the cycles in which the breaker tripped; the ground tally; and a balance line: starting charge plus everything fed in, against what is on the chain plus the ground tally.
Six forms down the chute: form 1 under the hopper, form 6 at the end.
Start: 3, 6, 6, 2, 2, 1 (nothing says quantities are whole numbers or never negative)
Upper mark: 7, 6, 9, 5, 7, 5
Lower mark: 3, 2, 4, 2, 3, 2
Start: 3, 6, 6, 2, 2, 1 ... Everything starts GREEN.
Over 38, halve every form, rounded down, and what comes off is waste. (the 38 limit is stated, but the waste tally starting at 0 is absent)
A cycle is five steps, always in this order, and each step goes all the way down the line before the next one starts.
Each form takes its load off the sheet below. Nobody trims here; a form can sit over capacity for a moment.
Walk forms 1 to 6. Whatever's over capacity runs down the chute into the next form before you get to that one
runs down the chute into the next form before you get to that one, so one heavy form can push the whole line.
Form 6 overtops into the waste pit.
A GREEN form at or above its upper mark goes HOT.
A HOT form at or below its lower mark goes back to GREEN.
Anywhere between, it stays what it was. Log every change.
Read all six first, then move mix.
GREEN loses a quarter, rounded down, to evaporation: waste.
HOT bleeds half, rounded down, back up the chute into the form before it; form 1's bleed goes to waste.
Nothing trims after this, so a form can carry over capacity into the next charge, or finish the run that way.
Total the line. Over 38, halve every form... 38 or under, leave it.
Over 38, halve every form, rounded down, and what comes off is waste. ... the cycles in which a washout fired

the quantity in forms 1 to 6, in order; the end state of each form (GREEN or HOT); every state change as (cycle, form, before, after); the cycles in which a washout fired; the waste tally; and a balance line: starting mix plus all charges, against what is in the forms plus waste.
Six crucibles, 1 at the charging end, 6 at the tapping end.
Whole units of melt; any split rounds down. (non-negativity not stated)
Working volume: 10, 8, 12, 6, 9, 7
Upper mark: 7, 6, 9, 5, 7, 5
Lower mark: 3, 2, 4, 2, 3, 2
Starting melt: 3, 6, 6, 2, 2, 1 Everything starts BASE.
Line limit for the emergency tap: 38. ... Slag tally: everything that reached the pit.
Five moves per cycle, each finished down the whole line before the next.
Charge. Pour the row in; nobody watches volume while charging.
Walk 1 to 6. Anything over working volume runs down the launder into the next crucible before you judge that one
runs down the launder into the next crucible before you judge that one, so it can chain.
Overflow off 6 goes to the slag pit.
A BASE crucible at or above its upper mark goes SUPERHEATED.
A SUPERHEATED one at or below its lower mark drops back to BASE.
In between, it holds. Log every change.
Bleed. Read all six before touching any.
BASE crucibles skim a quarter to slag.
SUPERHEATED crucibles send half back up the return launder to the crucible before them; crucible 1 has nowhere to send it, so its half goes to slag.
A crucible can finish over volume; that waits for next cycle's overflow, and after cycle 5 it stays.
Emergency tap. Total the line. Strictly over 38
halve every crucible, removed melt to slag, log the cycle.

the melt in crucibles 1 to 6, in order; each crucible's state (BASE or SUPERHEATED); every change as (cycle, crucible, before, after); the cycles in which an emergency tap fired; the slag tally; and a balance line: starting melt plus all charges, against what is in the crucibles plus slag.
The stem run is six segments, 1 at the root collar, 6 at the crown.
Sap is counted in whole units, and every segment opens QUIET. (non-negativity not stated)
Holding volume: 10 8 12 6 9 7
Upper mark: 7 6 9 5 7 5
Lower mark: 3 2 4 2 3 2
every segment opens QUIET. ... Sap at start: 3 6 6 2 2 1
Leaf-drop threshold, whole stem: 38 ... Loss tally: everything transpired, respired or sent past the collar, starting from zero.
Each cycle has five moves, always in this order. Finish the whole stem before you start the next move.
Feed. Add the row. Don't check volume yet.
Push, from 1 up to 6. Anything over a segment's volume goes up the xylem into the next segment before you reach it
goes up the xylem into the next segment before you reach it, so one surge can ride the whole stem.
Whatever goes over the top of 6 is transpired.
A QUIET segment at or above its upper mark goes SINK-ACTIVE.
A SINK-ACTIVE segment at or below its lower mark goes QUIET.
Between the marks it stays as it was. Log every flip.
Work out every amount from the sap in place before anything moves.
QUIET respires a quarter. ... Round down both.
SINK-ACTIVE sends half down the phloem to the segment below. ... What segment 1 sends goes to the roots and off our books.
Volume isn't checked here, so a segment can sit overfull until next cycle's push. After cycle 5 it stays that way.
If the stem totals over 38 (exactly 38 doesn't count)
halve every segment, rounding down. What comes off is transpired. ... the cycles in which leaf-drop fired

sap in segments 1 to 6, in order; the state of each segment; every flip as (cycle, segment, before, after); the cycles in which leaf-drop fired; the loss tally; and a balance line: sap at start plus everything fed in, against sap standing plus the tally.
Six compartments, 1 at the bow through 6 at the stern.
Water counts in whole units, never below zero.
Inception marks: 7, 6, 9, 5, 7, 5
Desinence marks: 3, 2, 4, 2, 3, 2
Every pump starts LAMINAR. ... Water at start: 3, 6, 6, 2, 2, 1
Emergency blow threshold, whole hull: 38. ... Keep one running overboard total from zero
Each cycle is five steps, in order, each finished in all six before the next.
Flood. Add the cycle's water. Don't stop at the volume; let it overfill.
Work bow to stern, 1 through 6. Anything above volume runs aft into the next compartment, leaving this one exactly full.
Since 1 goes before 2, one surge can carry down the whole line.
Whatever overtops 6 goes overboard.
LAMINAR at or above its inception mark goes CAVITATING.
CAVITATING only settles to LAMINAR at or below its desinence mark
in between, it holds. Log every change. (single pass per step; at-most-once is implied by one reading per cycle)
Size every discharge off current readings before touching a valve ... Then open them all together.
LAMINAR moves a quarter, CAVITATING half, rounded down. ... LAMINAR water goes overboard.
CAVITATING water backflows forward into the next compartment toward the bow; out of 1 it goes overboard.
Nobody watches volume here, so a compartment can sit overfull until next cycle's scuppers, and after cycle 5 it stays that way.
Sum all six. Strictly over 38: ... At 38 or under, leave it.
every compartment halves, rounded down, the difference overboard; note the cycle.

water in compartments 1 to 6, in order; the state of each pump (LAMINAR or CAVITATING); every state change as (cycle, compartment, before, after); the cycles in which a blow fired; the overboard tally; and a balance line: water at start plus everything flooded in, against water aboard plus overboard.
Six chambers: 1 at the head, 6 at the tail.
Nutrient mass is whole units; any split rounds down. (non-negativity not stated)
Chamber limits, 1 to 6: 10, 8, 12, 6, 9, 7.
Pupation marks: 7, 6, 9, 5, 7, 5.
Fallback marks: 3, 2, 4, 2, 3, 2.
Starting mass: 3, 6, 6, 2, 2, 1. Every chamber starts LARVAL.
Above 38, every chamber halves ... Keep one loss tally: tail overflow, burn-off, chamber 1's reabsorbed half, moult sheddings. (the tally's starting value of 0 is not stated)
Finish each job along the whole line before the next:
1. Feed. Add the cycle's ration: ... No trimming yet.
Walk from 1 to 6. Anything above a chamber's limit moves into the next chamber
so overflow can cascade down the line.
Chamber 6's overflow is discarded. ... Keep one loss tally: tail overflow,
A LARVAL chamber at or above its pupation mark goes PUPAL.
A PUPAL chamber at or below its fallback mark goes back to LARVAL
Anything in between holds its stage. Log every change as (cycle, chamber, before, after).
Weigh all six first, then act.
LARVAL chambers burn off a quarter of their mass. ... Keep one loss tally: ... burn-off
PUPAL chambers reabsorb half back into the chamber ahead (one number lower); chamber 1's half is discarded.
No trimming: a chamber can stay over limit until next cycle's overflow, or for good after cycle 5.
Total the line. Above 38, every chamber halves and the shed mass is discarded. At 38 or under, leave it.
Above 38, every chamber halves and the shed mass is discarded. ... moult sheddings. ... the cycles in which a moult fired

mass in chambers 1 to 6, in order; the stage of each chamber (LARVAL or PUPAL); every stage change as (cycle, chamber, before, after); the cycles in which a moult fired; the loss tally; and a balance line: mass at start plus all feed, against mass in the chambers plus the tally.
Six tanks in series, 1 at the inlet, 6 at the outfall.
We count whole units of liquor, rounding down on every split.
Upper marks: 7, 6, 9, 5, 7, 5.
Lower marks: 3, 2, 4, 2, 3, 2.
Starting contents: 3, 6, 6, 2, 2, 1. All start STEADY.
Storm bypass limit, whole line: 38. ... The outfall tally takes everything sent to outfall.
Each cycle, five jobs in order, each finished down the whole line before the next
Inflow. Add the row. A tank can sit over volume for now.
Weirs. Walk 1 to 6. Anything over volume goes over the weir into the next tank before you look at that one
goes over the weir into the next tank before you look at that one, so a surge can ride down the line.
Tank 6 overflows to outfall.
States. STEADY at or above the upper mark goes OVERLOADED.
OVERLOADED at or below the lower mark comes back STEADY.
Between the marks, no change. Log every change.
Work out every tank's draw from what it holds now, then move it all at once.
STEADY: a quarter to outfall.
OVERLOADED: half back up the return line to the tank before; tank 1's return goes to outfall.
Return flow can leave a tank over volume; the weirs take it next cycle, and after cycle 5 it stays.
Storm bypass. Total the line. Strictly over 38
every tank keeps half, rounded down; the rest goes to outfall. ... the cycles in which the bypass fired

the contents of tanks 1 to 6, in order; each tank's state (STEADY or OVERLOADED); every change as (cycle, tank, before, after); the cycles in which the bypass fired; the outfall tally; and a balance line: starting contents plus all inflow, against what is in the tanks plus outfall.
The stack is six retrieval buffers: tier 1 sits next to the LLM, tier 6 furthest out.
Everything you track is chunks held.
COLD mark: 3, 2, 4, 2, 3, 2
Holding at start: 3, 6, 6, 2, 2, 1 ... Every tier starts COLD.
Context ceiling for the whole stack: 38. ... Keep one running drop count covering tier-6 evictions, compactions, tier-1 promotions and resets.
A cycle is five passes, each finished across the whole stack before the next starts.
Load. Add the cycle's new chunks. No trimming yet; a tier can sit over budget here.
Evict. Walk tier 1 through 6. Anything over budget moves out to the next tier
so it can push that tier over before you reach it.
Overflow from tier 6 is dropped.
A COLD tier at or above its HOT mark goes HOT
a HOT tier at or below its COLD mark goes COLD.
Anywhere between the marks, it keeps its flag. Log every flip.
Off the post-flag counts ... Work out all six amounts before moving anything.
a COLD tier compacts a quarter of its chunks (round down), dropped
a HOT tier promotes half (round down) into the tier one closer to the LLM, and tier 1's promotion is dropped.
A promotion can leave a tier over budget; that waits for next cycle's evict, and after cycle 5 it just stands.
If the stack totals more than 38, context reset ... Exactly 38 is fine.
every tier halves (round down), removed chunks dropped. ... the cycles in which a reset fired

holdings in tiers 1 to 6, in order; the state of each tier (COLD or HOT); every flip as (cycle, tier, before, after); the cycles in which a reset fired; the dropped tally; and a balance line: chunks at start plus everything loaded, against chunks held plus dropped.
six nonnegative integer components, positions 1 to 6 ... Projection sweep, Gauss-Seidel, 1 through 6 ... push the violation into x_{i+1}
six nonnegative integer components, positions 1 to 6
Activation thresholds u = (7, 6, 9, 5, 7, 5)
deactivation thresholds d = (3, 2, 4, 2, 3, 2)
starting at x0 = (3, 6, 6, 2, 2, 1) ... every component starts INACTIVE
Budget on the 1-norm: 38. Slack s starts at 0
Each cycle is five steps, and each step finishes across the whole vector before the next one starts.
Load. Add the cycle's row of b to x. Bounds are not enforced here.
Clip x_i to c_i and push the violation into x_{i+1} before you visit it, so overflow cascades down the vector.
push the violation into x_{i+1} before you visit it, so overflow cascades down the vector
Component 6's violation goes to s.
Active-set update on the projected x. INACTIVE goes ACTIVE at x_i >= u_i
ACTIVE drops back to INACTIVE at x_i <= d_i
Anywhere in between, the flag holds. Log every flip as (cycle, position, before, after).
Jacobi shed. Compute all six amounts from the same x before anything moves.
An INACTIVE component sheds floor(x_i/4) to s.
An ACTIVE component moves floor(x_i/2) up to x_{i-1}; component 1 sends its share to s.
No projection after this step: a component can sit over its bound until the next sweep, and after cycle 5 it simply stays there.
If the 1-norm is strictly above 38
halve every component with floor and book what came off to s. Note the cycle.

the vector x, components 1 to 6, in order; each component's flag (INACTIVE or ACTIVE); every flip as (cycle, component, before, after); the cycles in which the penalty fired; the slack s; and a balance line: the starting 1-norm plus everything loaded, against the final 1-norm plus s.

Escalate at: 7, 6, 9, 5, 7, 5
Stand down at: 3, 2, 4, 2, 3, 2
Open at start: 3, 6, 6, 2, 2, 1 ... Everyone starts ROUTINE.
The board target is 38 open tickets. ... Every closure, by any route, goes on one closed tally, from zero.
Each cycle runs five steps, each finished board-wide before the next.
New tickets land (per cycle, teams 1 to 6) ... Limits don't bite yet.
Walk the line, team 1 to team 6. A team's excess goes to the next team down
A team's excess goes to the next team down, counting when you reach them.
Team 6's overflow is closed-without-action.
A ROUTINE team at or above its escalation mark goes ESCALATED
an ESCALATED team at or below its stand-down mark goes back to ROUTINE.
In between, status holds. Log every flip. (nothing says a team changes at most once per cycle)
Work the queues off one snapshot.
A ROUTINE team closes a quarter of its tickets, rounded down. ... Every closure, by any route, goes on one closed tally
An ESCALATED team bounces half, rounded down, to the team upstream; team 1 has nobody upstream, so its bounce is closed.
Bounced tickets can leave a team over its limit until the next walk; after cycle 5 they stay.
Total the board. Strictly over 38, every team keeps half its tickets, rounded down ... At 38 or under, leave it.
every team keeps half its tickets, rounded down, and the rest are closed-without-action. ... the cycles in which the backlog cut fired

open tickets for teams 1 to 6, in order; each team's status (ROUTINE or ESCALATED); every status change as (cycle, team, before, after); the cycles in which the backlog cut fired; the closed tally; and a balance line: tickets at start plus everything that arrived, against tickets open plus tickets closed.

Lower threshold: 3, 2, 4, 2, 3, 2
Starting charge: 3, 6, 6, 2, 2, 1 ... All stages start CLEAR

Five cycles, five steps each, in this order. Each step finishes everywhere before the next starts.

Go 1 to 6 in turn. A stage over rating drops to exactly its rating and passes the excess to the next stage toward the load
passes the excess to the next stage toward the load before that one is checked, so excess can cascade in one pass

ASSERTED at or below lower goes CLEAR
in between, it holds. States change only here, at most once per cycle.

ASSERTED instead sends half, rounded down, back through the return diode to the stage just before it, toward the source; stage 1's feedback goes to ground.

Every cycle, if the six total strictly above 38, it trips ... At 38 or below, nothing.
each stage keeps half, rounded down; the rest goes to ground.

HOT bleeds half, rounded down, back up the chute into the form before it (5 into 4). Form 1's bleed is waste.

Total all six. Strictly over 38: ... Otherwise nothing.
each form keeps half, rounded down; the rest is waste; note the cycle.

the six end quantities, positions 1 to 6; the six end states; every state change as (cycle, position, before, after); the cycles the washout fired; the loss tally; and the balance check: starting mix plus all pours must equal end quantities plus loss tally.
